newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki scrapes higher then mixed, eyes U.S..
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki scrapes higher then mixed, eyes U.S..

text.p: Shares started higher, nudging new all-time highs then turned mixed in thin volume on Monday, with Nokia building on Friday's gains in above 400.00 markka territory, brokers said.
"This looks fairly firm, but thin," one broker said, adding that, with many domestic players on summer holiday, the trend would depend on a direction from U.S. players later on.

Nokia A traded up 1.20 markka at 404.00 after touching 407.00 in modest 29 million markka volume. Brokers said it looked likely to find a new trading range above 400.00 after crossing that threshold for the first time on Friday.
Brokers said position-taking ahead of rival Motorola's second-quarter earnings report, due after the close on Tuesday, could trigger some speculative activity.

UPM-Kymmene added 0.60 markka to 127.50 in meagre volume. Enso rose 0.20 to 49.50, but Metsa-Serla fell 0.80 to 45.00 in thin trade. Brokers said Finnish forestries were attracting attention abroad ahead of interim reports from big U.S. papermakers. The options exchange marked up its benchmark pulp price to $572.30/tonne from $569.70.
Merita fell 0.20 markka to 19.70 in slim trade, failing to return above 20.00 markka as last week.
